title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report analyzes 347 support tickets to evaluate cost, speed, reopening rates, satisfaction, and agent concentration. The total labor cost was $27,422.90. Key findings indicate that the Beta team incurred the highest costs, chat resolution times were the slowest, and email tickets had a significantly higher reopening rate than chat tickets. A small segment of high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets was identified, and agent workload concentration appears moderate.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 347 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.2 minutes and a total labor cost of $27,422.90.
Team labor costs ranked as follows: Beta ($10,247.36), Gamma ($9,387.73), Alpha ($7,787.81).
Mean resolution times by channel ranked as follows: chat (83.0 minutes), email (73.0 minutes), phone (69.3 minutes).
The email reopening rate (17.2%) was 119.8% higher than the chat reopening rate (7.8%), indicating a significant increase in reopenings for email compared to chat.
There were 12 tickets identified as high-cost and low-satisfaction, representing a critical segment with an 8.3% reopening rate.
Resolution times had a median of 65.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.9 minutes. The average satisfaction score was 4.15, with 19 tickets missing satisfaction data.
The support team consists of 18 unique agents. The top agent handled 26 tickets, accounting for 7.5% of the total workload.

limitations: Satisfaction scores were missing for 19 tickets, which may bias the satisfaction mean.
The analysis assumes the 'cleaned.csv' data is accurate and representative of current operations.
The 'high-cost low-satisfaction' segment is small (12 tickets), so conclusions there should be drawn cautiously.
conclusion: The analysis highlights significant variations in cost and performance across teams and channels. The high reopening rate for email tickets compared to chat suggests a potential area for process improvement. While agent workload is not heavily concentrated, monitoring the high-cost, low-satisfaction segment could prevent value leakage.
